description_full: SK hynix Inc. through its subsidiaries, engages in research, develops, manufactures, distributes, and sells semiconductor devices in Korea, China, rest of Asia, the United States, Europe, and internationally. It offers DRAM, such as server memory, graphics memory, mobile memory, PC memory, consumer memory; NAND flash memory; SSD; and MCP products. It also engages in foundry business, produces non-memory semiconductors. The company serves its products for server, networking, mobile, personal computer, consumer, and automotive applications. The company was formerly known as Hynix Semiconductor Inc. and changed its name to SK hynix Inc. in March 2012. SK hynix Inc. was incorporated in 1949 and is headquartered in Icheon-si, South Korea.
ceo_bio: Dr. Noh-Jung  Kwak | President, CEO & Executive Director | Age 60 | Compensation: $3.2M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 47K people. Revenue per employee of $1.5M ranks in the top quartile among Technology peers. Each employee generates $390K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $7K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 2× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). R&D investment of 7% of revenue (moderate) signals commitment to product development and talent.
financial_summary: SK hynix Inc. is a mega-cap technology business with a $929.3B market cap on $72.8B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +25% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +11.1pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 14% against a 13% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, with gross margins sitting at 42%.

The business throws off $18.6B in free cash flow — roughly 26 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.24× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 51× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 0.1%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 2.1× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
